bibliography.abstract: In this paper, we analyze the dispatch-level feasibility of introducing premium membership into an on-demand taxi-sharing service using a sequential optimal insertion method. We propose two dispatch-level methods: deadline shortening for premium users, and deadline shortening with dedicated premium vehicles. We compare them with a baseline dispatch method through SUMO-based simulations under three demand scenarios: steady uniform demand, time-varying demand with a peak period, and urban-focused demand with concentrated peak traffic. Our results show that the suitable priority mechanism depends on operating conditions and premium ratio, suggesting that condition-dependent method switching may provide premium benefits while keeping non-premium-user burden smaller for overall optimization.
bibliography.title: Evaluating Priority Dispatch for Premium Membership in On-demand Taxi-sharing

en.caveats: Findings are based on synthetic traffic simulations rather than field trials or empirical dispatch data from an operating ride-hailing platform.
en.what: SUMO-based traffic simulations evaluated two dispatch mechanisms for premium taxi-sharing memberships: deadline shortening for subscribers, and deadline shortening combined with dedicated premium vehicles. The performance of these strategies was tested against a standard baseline across uniform, peak-hour, and spatially concentrated high-density demand profiles.
en.why: The analysis demonstrates that fleet managers cannot rely on a single priority rule; maximizing service quality for subscribers while minimizing performance drops for standard riders requires switching dispatch strategies based on real-time travel demand and subscriber proportions.
